archiveTitle: Daily Brief | Seikyu: Let's Go! reveals four-player campervan trips

entries.headline: Seikyu: Let's Go! announced with up to four-player campervan trips
entries.summary: AUTOMATON reports that ACE Entertainment announced the PC (Steam) campervan travel game on September 28. Players take the roles of yokai visiting Seikyu Island and divide driving, navigation, photography and campsite duties. The game is planned to support up to four players and proximity voice chat.

entries.headline: テニスの王子様: The Prince of Tennis remasters reveal DLC trailers and release dates
entries.summary: Denfaminicogamer reports that Konami has released trailers for additional DLC for two romance-game remasters. The Ryoga Echizen DLC for Gakuensai no Ojisama is planned for October 15, while the Hikaru Zaizen DLC for Doki Doki Survival is planned for November 13. Both feature new scenarios and newly drawn illustrations.

entries.headline: みすずの国: Misuzu no Kuni feature examines belonging in an imagined tengu society
entries.summary: A newly published AUTOMATON feature examines the visual novel created by Kazuki and STUDIO HOMMAGE. It discusses how an imagined tengu society portrays minority experiences and life continuing beyond unexpected circumstances. This is coverage of new critical analysis, rather than a new release announcement.

entries.headline: Onimusha: Way of the Sword feature explores period-drama storytelling and combat choices
entries.summary: A newly published AUTOMATON hands-on feature examines how Onimusha: Way of the Sword carries forward period-drama storytelling and performance, while allowing personal combat experiences through different actions. The author describes how the same encounter can be approached through different defensive and offensive techniques. These are observations by the writer, rather than an announcement of new content.

entries.headline: MindsEye developer's parent enters administration; project plans remain unclear
entries.summary: AUTOMATON reported on September 28 that Build A Rocket Boy Ltd, the group's parent company, entered UK administration on September 23. Administrators take control of its assets and evaluate continued operation, a sale or asset disposal. Administration does not establish that liquidation is certain. Plans for MindsEye, EVERYWHERE and ARCADIA remain unclear.
